title: Two Weber Street East high-rise developments advance
subtitle: Ground-floor commercial space, traffic, parks, affordable housing contributions and three-bedroom units were raised on both Weber Street East proposals.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee held public meetings on two Weber Street East redevelopment proposals and recommended both for approval. The first covers 1157 and 1175 Weber Street East, the former car dealership site, where a commercial designation would change to mixed use to allow two towers on a four-storey podium. The second covers 1770 King Street East and 815 and 825 Weber Street East, where a 27-storey rental building is proposed near the Highway 8 entrance to downtown.

For the second site, the committee added a requirement for commercial space on the ground floor. This responds to concerns that existing businesses would be removed and the corner would be left without shops or services for new residents. Staff will work with the applicant to set the minimum non-residential floor area, and further public notice was waived.

Both recommendations go to Council for a final decision, and the official plan amendments also need Region of Waterloo approval. Staff are to report back to Council on details of the ground-floor commercial space. One councillor declared a conflict of interest on an item numbered 6.1 that was not on the agenda for this meeting.

decisions.item: 1157 and 1175 Weber Street East official plan change
decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the change from Commercial to Mixed Use for M.K.G. Holding Corporation's site and sending it to the Region of Waterloo for approval {{vote:m1}}.
The committee recommended approving the zoning by-law amendment for the proposed mixed-use development.

decisions.item: Urban Design Brief for Weber Street site
decisions.detail: The committee recommended endorsing the March 2023 Urban Design Brief and directing staff to apply it through future site plan approval.

decisions.item: 1770 King Street East official plan change
decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the change to Special Policy Area 11 to permit a 27-storey multiple dwelling development, forwarded to the Region of Waterloo {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended approving the zoning by-law amendment for King Weber Kitchener Holdings Inc.

The committee recommended special regulations requiring ground-floor commercial space with 4.5-metre ceilings, allowing dwellings alongside it, and a minimum non-residential floor area to be set by staff with the applicant.
The committee recommended that further notice not be required for the amended 1770 King Street East zoning by-law amendment.

debate: On the Weber Street site, a delegate for the applicant said neighbourhood concerns about height, traffic, parking, park space and density were addressed by lowering the podium from five to four storeys, adding a second driveway, and providing rooftop and private outdoor amenity space.

One councillor raised concern about traffic backing up near the Franklin Street access. The applicant's consultant said the Region and the Ministry of Transportation reviewed it closely and that the proposed location met their standards. The parking podium facing the expressway was described as acting as a noise barrier.

Councillors asked about affordability on both projects. The Weber Street applicant proposed a $350,000 donation to a local affordable housing provider instead of on-site units. The King Street applicant said its building would be mid-market rental and not deeply affordable.

On the King Street site, councillors were concerned that removing an existing plaza would leave a high-density area near a high school with no nearby shops. The applicant said ground-floor units could convert to retail, and councillors pushed for a firmer commitment.

Other points on the King Street proposal included a request to explore three-bedroom units given nearby schools, questions about the shadow study and its effect on Rockway Gardens, traffic from nearby developments, and reduced parkland funding under provincial Bill 23.
